entries.title: Morning Briefing · 23 November 2026
headlines: Russian strikes kill at least 15 across the Kyiv region
NATO meets in Brussels today as Poland says all three objects were Russian Kh-101 missiles
Asian stocks slide on the AI rout as US futures bounce about 2%
Iran claims control of Hormuz and readies 14 tankers to test the US blockade
New Zealand bat out a draw in the Wellington Test against India

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 15 across the Kyiv region
stories.summary: Overnight strikes hit several towns around Kyiv. In Dymer at least 11 people died when part of a five-storey block collapsed, with 11 still being searched for, including two children. A supermarket strike in Vyshneve killed three and injured 15, and one person died in Bila Tserkva.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll has risen sharply since yesterday's report of three deaths, as Kyiv presses Washington for more Patriot systems.

stories.headline: NATO meets today as Poland says all three objects were Kh-101 missiles
stories.summary: A preliminary finding by the Lublin prosecutor's office says the three objects that entered Polish airspace on Friday were all Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles; Warsaw first described two missiles and a drone. The North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels today, and Mark Rutte said NATO would defend every inch of Polish territory.
stories.whyItMatters: Three confirmed Russian cruise missiles on NATO soil is the most serious incursion of the war so far, and today's meeting will show how hard the alliance responds.

stories.headline: Iran claims control of Hormuz and readies 14 tankers to test the US blockade
stories.summary: Iran says ships must negotiate passage through the Strait of Hormuz with its authorities and is reported to be preparing 14 oil tankers to run the US naval blockade. Bahrain intercepted more Iranian attacks on Sunday with no new injuries, and UKMTO reported two tankers damaged. Trump said US military action would resume after the New Year unless there is a deal.
stories.whyItMatters: A tanker convoy meeting US warships is the clearest route to a direct clash and keeps an oil-price risk over markets.

stories.headline: Cutting Costs Bill heads to Parliament on Thursday
stories.summary: The bill that puts Friday's UK-EU package into law, including food-standards alignment and linking to the EU carbon market from 2028, is due before MPs on Thursday. Andy Burnham ended his European trip with talks with Dutch PM Rob Jetten. The Conservatives say the deal will raise energy bills, and universities warn about lower fees for EU students.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the first Commons test of the EU reset, and the student-fees dispute has a six-month deadline attached.

stories.headline: Modi and Nepal's Balendra Shah hold talks at Hyderabad House
stories.summary: Delegation-level talks began this morning after a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Expected outcomes include a joint vision document, MoUs on education, health, agriculture and disaster management, new connectivity and energy projects, and a virtual flag-off of the Saryu-Kamala Express. Nothing had been signed at the time of writing.
stories.whyItMatters: It is Shah's first state visit, and the deals will show how far India can rebuild ties with Nepal's new government, including flood-reconstruction aid.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules over the weekend
stories.summary: GOV.UK still lists HC 584 (3 September 2026) as the latest Statement of Changes. Earned settlement (10-year ILR) remains policy only, with no rules laid and no start date. Already confirmed: student maintenance amounts rise for applications made from 30 November, and the Immigration and Asylum Bill is now in the Lords.

stories.headline: Wellington Test drawn as New Zealand hold out
stories.summary: New Zealand finished on 239/5 after 120 overs, still 113 behind India's 720/9 declared. Daryl Mitchell (49 not out off 186 balls) and Glenn Phillips (26 not out off 126) shared an unbroken stand of 63 on a flat Basin Reserve pitch.
stories.whyItMatters: The series is level at 0-0 going into the second Test at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, from Friday 27 November.

stories.headline: Shenzhou-24 expected to fly Pakistan's first astronaut
stories.summary: China's next crewed mission is unofficially set to launch from Jiuquan at about 00:19 GMT on Wednesday 25 November, carrying a Pakistani astronaut. China has not confirmed the date; Pakistan has pointed to 25 November.
stories.whyItMatters: It would be the first foreign astronaut aboard China's Tiangong station.

stories.headline: This week: first Hera images of Dimorphos, and a Cygnus cargo launch
stories.summary: ESA releases Hera's first images of the asteroid Dimorphos on Wednesday at 18:45 GMT. NASA briefs today on the NG-25 Cygnus resupply mission, due to launch to the ISS on a Falcon 9 on Sunday 29 November at 15:49 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: Hera is studying the asteroid NASA's DART probe struck in 2022, to measure how well the planetary-defence test worked.

stories.headline: Asia sells off on the AI rout while US futures rebound
stories.summary: Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before trading 3.2% lower at 04:30 GMT; Hong Kong and mainland China were down about 0.6%, Taiwan rose 2.5% and Japan is shut. At 02:32 GMT US futures were up: S&P 500 1.96%, Dow 1.54%, Nasdaq-100 2.33%. Friday 20 Nov closes: S&P 500 6,910.39 (down 3.70%), Dow 48,147.33 (down 1.93%), Nasdaq Composite 22,617.73 (down 5.28%).
stories.whyItMatters: Fears over AI spending, turmoil at Nvidia and bets on another Fed rate rise drove last week's losses. Brent was near 92 dollars and gold near 3,600 dollars.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty give up early gains (live, 09:46 IST)
stories.summary: Indian shares opened higher, with the Sensex up 0.78% at 84,571, then reversed. At 09:46 IST, still trading, the Sensex was down 0.64% at 83,383.75 and the Nifty 50 down 0.69% at 25,623.00, with metal and bank stocks down about 2% and IT up about 1%.
stories.whyItMatters: Friday's nine-month highs are being tested by the global tech sell-off. Some live blogs say Indian markets will be shut on Tuesday, which is not yet confirmed with the exchanges.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 starts the week at a five-month low
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed Friday 20 Nov down 1.02% at 10,346.34, its fifth straight fall and about 5% lower on the week, with miners, banks and defence stocks weakest. London opens at 08:00 GMT; firmer US futures point to a steadier start.
stories.whyItMatters: London has followed the global tech-led sell-off despite holding few tech stocks, so commodity prices and banks will set the tone today.
